topic: A roadside dhaba serves the best tea on the highway at night, but by morning there is only an empty field.

episode.title: Midnight Watch: The Dhaba That Vanished

shots.narration: The tea was perfect; by sunrise, the dhaba was gone.
shots.scene: Vertical 9:16, 3D animated film look, old Pakistani haveli courtyard at night, brass lantern beside a plain clay teacup, no writing anywhere.
shots.action: Bashir slides the clay teacup toward Saad.
shots.mood: Warm lantern glow surrounded by deep blue shadows.

shots.narration: Bashir Chacha told Saad how he found it last winter.
shots.scene: Haveli courtyard, Bashir in his brown woollen shawl and white cap opposite Saad in his dark green hoodie.
shots.action: Bashir points toward the distant highway.
shots.mood: Low fog beyond the courtyard wall, still moonlit air.

shots.narration: [whispers] One warm window shone beside an otherwise empty highway.
shots.scene: Flashback, isolated Pakistani roadside dhaba with a mud courtyard, woven charpoy and warm window, no signs or markings.
shots.action: Bashir approaches the glowing doorway with his brass lantern.
shots.mood: Welcoming amber light isolated in vast cold darkness.

shots.narration: Inside, a steaming cup waited, but nobody was there.
shots.scene: Empty dhaba interior with rough plaster walls, one wooden table and a steaming clay teacup.
shots.mood: Soft steam, amber lamplight, unnaturally empty corners.

shots.narration: Then the kettle moved without a hand.
shots.scene: Dhaba counter beside Bashir, plain metal kettle with no markings, empty space behind the counter.
shots.action: The kettle slides across the counter toward Bashir.
shots.mood: Long crooked shadows beneath a motionless hanging lamp.

shots.narration: [surprised] Every empty chair turned toward him.
shots.scene: Dhaba interior, Bashir beside the table holding his clay cup, three empty wooden chairs around him.
shots.action: The three chairs swivel toward Bashir.
shots.mood: Tight pools of light, black doorway, looming chair backs.

shots.narration: He hurried outside, still holding that unfinished tea.
shots.scene: Dhaba doorway opening onto an empty highway, lantern glow and pale fog.
shots.action: Bashir backs through the doorway carrying the cup.
shots.mood: Cold moonlight swallowing the warm interior glow.

shots.narration: At dawn, he returned to an empty field.
shots.scene: Same roadside location at dawn, bare grass where the dhaba stood, matching roadside tree and distant hills.
shots.action: Bashir parts the tall grass with his lantern.
shots.mood: Pale dawn fog, untouched grass, no building or foundations.

shots.scene: Empty roadside field in dawn light, close view of Bashir's grey beard, brown shawl and clay cup.
shots.action: A thin ribbon of steam rises from Bashir's cup.
shots.mood: Frosty blue surroundings against impossible warm steam.

shots.narration: Back beside the lantern, Saad found the cup empty.
shots.scene: Present-night haveli courtyard, same plain cup beside Bashir's brass lantern, Saad's small torch on the table.
shots.action: Saad tilts the empty cup toward the lantern.
shots.mood: Quiet amber light, dark courtyard arches behind both listeners.

shots.narration: Above them, the dhaba's kettle tipped out of thin air.
shots.scene: Haveli courtyard, familiar metal kettle suspended above the table without support, Bashir and Saad beneath it.
shots.action: The floating kettle pours steaming tea into the cup.
shots.mood: Huge kettle shadow across the wall, pale steam surrounding frozen faces.

shots.narration: [whispers] Tomorrow, we visit the station this key unlocks.
shots.scene: Lantern-lit courtyard table, clay cup holding tea and a large unmarked antique railway key.
shots.action: Saad lifts the dripping key from the cup.
shots.mood: Brass highlights, curling steam, deep darkness beyond the table.

episode.endHook: A key inside the teacup leads to an abandoned railway station.
episode.description: By lantern light, Bashir Chacha tells Saad about a roadside dhaba with unforgettable tea—and no trace by sunrise. But some cups should never be brought home. A fictional spooky tale from Midnight Watch.
